subject: One small original environment sprite for a top-down 16-bit pixel-art RPG: an old brown fallen hollow woodland log, back left cut end receding and near right broken open end facing the viewer, only slightly diagonal (almost horizontal). A jagged pale exposed-wood rim around the dark hollow; a few crooked broken twigs; a single soft clump of sage moss folded over the upper left rim and two small tiers of rust-orange bracket fungi. Weathered bark suggested by TWO OR THREE LONG chunky angular grooves, NOT tiny stippling. Invent the sprite as native 64 by 32 square pixels, the whole composition pixel perfect. Bold irregular connected patches five or six pixels across, dark indigo-purple inland contours, warm muted brown bark midtones, blue-purple lower shade, a few golden tan cut-wood pixels, sage moss. A small 12-18-color palette, pure flat pixel clusters, hard staircase edges. High-quality intentional 1990s handheld/SNES adventure tileset sprite, not a 3D render, not a miniature painting. Every virtual pixel is magnified as an identical crisp square; create a hard pixel grid, no antialias, no soft glow/no blur. Isolated single log with small attached shelf fungi, no grass mat, no ground, no drop shadow, no writing, no border, no UI. Light is neutral, not a baked moonbeam. Use UNIFORM SOLID MAGENTA #ff00ff background exclusively outside the item for clean keying, never inside the bark/lichen. Sprite centered, with margins all around, wide landscape orientation. Imagine one logical 96x64 canvas scaled up exactly: log covers 69-72 columns and 28-32 rows, not the full canvas. Strong silhouette designed to be readable at native 64 px wide.
